title: I wanted a serious game less depressing than DEFCON, so I built FOGLINE with AI. Looking for beta testers
author: DueSpkyke
selftext:
Hi everyone,

DEFCON is one of the games that inspired me, but its tagline says it all: "Everybody dies." I wanted to keep the tension of that big, cold situation map while making something less depressing. In FOGLINE, you win by keeping a crisis under control, not by counting how many cities are left.

FOGLINE is a real-time strategy serious game that runs in the browser. You command a small force through fictional crises set on real maps.

How it plays

\- Each mission lasts about 8 to 11 minutes at normal speed

\- Alerts come in: a viral video, a cyberattack, a silent ship, a false alarm

\- You verify, then decide before the countdown ends (90 s on Easy, 30 s on Hard)

\- Many alerts are false, and reacting to the wrong one has a cost

\- The debrief reveals what was really happening and where your judgement failed

There are six regions and 74 missions, in English and French. There are no nukes and no city strikes, and all events are fictional. The idea comes from my article on cognitive warfare: the goal is to train decision-making under uncertainty.

\*\*How AI was used\*\*

I handled the concept, design decisions and playtesting direction. Claude wrote most of the code, helped draft the scenarios and built the automated test bots. Happy to answer questions about that workflow, including what went wrong.

\*\*Where I need help\*\*

It's still a prototype. So far it has mostly been tested by scripts, and bots can't tell me whether it's actually fun. I'm looking for beta testers, mainly for gameplay feedback:

\- Is it clear what to do in the first five minutes?

\- Is the pacing right, or are there dull stretches?

\- Do the 30-second decisions feel tense or just unfair?

\- Does the map stay readable when things get busy?

Any other feedback is welcome too: bugs, UI, phone play, or ideas for missions.

Play it here: [https://otakuch.github.io/fogline/](https://otakuch.github.io/fogline/)  


Thanks for reading. I'd really appreciate honest feedback, even if it's harsh.
